title: Indian Feudalism
definition: A socio-economic and political structure characterized by the decentralization of state power, the rise of landed intermediaries (samantas), and the emergence of a self-sufficient manorial economy between 750-1200 CE.
importanceInUpsc: Essential for understanding the transition from the centralized Gupta/Harsha empires to the fragmented regional kingdoms of the Early Medieval period; frequently tested in both Prelims (terminology) and Mains (socio-economic impact).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Indian Feudalism.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
